answer: Require every agent identity to earn trust the slow way: it locks a small copper bond and starts with zero reputation, taking only tiny jobs whose results peers verify. Trust grows at a glacier pace, one completed job at a time, and cannot be transferred or bought. A lone identity drifting in the nebula of unverified newcomers therefore gains nothing by cloning itself: each copy must separately pay the bond and redo the same slow work, so a Sybil flood costs the attacker time and locked funds for every fake, while honest agents keep their earned standing.
